result: {"findings": [{"file": "examples/cq_two_driver_misuse.zig", "line": 76, "severity": "major", "category": "tests", "title": "Exit-code contract inverted with no in-tree harness to update", "body": "The old contract was documented as \"a harness runs it and checks for a NON-zero exit\": failure was exit 0, and any non-zero exit meant the misuse was detected. The diff changes the failure signal from exit 0 to exit 3 and rewrites the header to say the harness must accept only the abort. Nothing in this tree implements or checks either rule — `grep` for `cq-two-driver-misuse` finds only build.zig and the example's own doc comment, and there is no tools/ or script directory. Mechanism: an existing external harness written against the previously documented rule tests `exit != 0`. Exit 3 satisfies that test. Consequence: the exact case the death test exists to catch (two drivers ran for the full 5 s window with no panic) is now reported as a pass by any consumer that follows the old, in-repo-documented rule, and the change ships no check that would catch the inversion. The contract is stated in prose only, at both ends, and neither end is verifiable from this repository."}, {"file": "examples/cq_spurious_select_repro.zig", "line": 52, "severity": "major", "category": "tests", "title": "The mutex changes the flooder's hot-loop timing that the reproducer depends on, and the doc's reproduction claim is not revalidated", "body": "The flooder's inner loop changes from a lock-free `feed_fd.load(.acquire)` plus a non-blocking `write` to `zio.Mutex.lock()` / `unlock()` on every iteration. `Mutex.lock` parks the task in the mutex wait queue on contention (src/sync/Mutex.zig:71,76) and `unlock` signals a waiter through the scheduler (src/sync/Mutex.zig:100-108). The driver takes the same mutex twice per generation, once of those while holding it across two `std.c.close` calls. This inserts new suspension and wake points into the exact flooder/driver interleaving that the module doc (lines 12-20) says the race needs. The header still carries the unmodified claim \"Reproduces within ~1 s on macOS/kqueue and Linux/io_uring, Debug and ReleaseSafe, with 8 workers\", and line 30 states \"Exit 0 = no reproduction within the budget\". Consequence: if the added synchronization widens or closes the publish-then-wake window, the program prints `clean:` and exits 0, which is byte-identical to a healthy run that simply did not hit the bug. A reproducer that has stopped reproducing reports the same result as a fixed bug, and the diff carries no evidence that the rate claim still holds after the change."}, {"file": "examples/cq_spurious_select_repro.zig", "line": 78, "severity": "minor", "category": "correctness", "title": "Both socketpair descriptors leak if the new fallible lock fails", "body": "Before the change, `defer _ = std.c.close(fds[0]); defer _ = std.c.close(fds[1]);` were registered immediately after `socketpair`, so no fallible call could run between creation and the close defer. The diff moves the closes into a combined defer at line 85 and inserts `try sh.feed_mu.lock()` at line 78, ahead of it. `Mutex.lock` returns `Cancelable!void`, so if the driver task is cancelled while parked on the mutex, the `try` returns `error.Canceled` from `driver` before the close defer exists. Both descriptors of that generation's socketpair leak, and the `errdefer` at line 98 does not cover them either because it only tears down the completion queue. Either register the close defer immediately after `socketpair` (separate from the `feed_fd` publication) or use `lockUncancelable()` for the publish, matching the teardown side."}, {"file": "build.zig", "line": 98, "severity": "minor", "category": "portability", "title": "Windows skip of a posix_only example is silent for the full examples build", "body": "The guard emits a `b.addFail` diagnostic only when `-Dexample=<name>` names the skipped example. For a plain `zig build examples` against a Windows target, the loop simply `continue`s: the example set silently shrinks by one and the step still reports success, with no message naming what was dropped. Mechanism: coverage narrows without any observable signal, so a Windows examples build reads exactly like a full one. If a second example is later marked `posix_only`, or if a future edit makes the flag apply more broadly, the shrinkage stays invisible. Emit the skip through `std.log`/`b.step` output in the `only_example == null` branch too, so the dropped names appear in the build log."}]}
